program_name: Ofoten Line (Ofotbanen) + Iron Ore Line (Malmbanan) Kiruna–Narvik Arctic heavy-haul ore corridor
program_type: Heavy-haul electrified iron-ore railway (Arctic freight backbone)
key_benefits: 43 km Norwegian section Narvik-Riksgränsen owned by Bane NOR + 398 km Malmbanan Riksgränsen-Boden owned by Trafikverket; single track electrified 15 kV 16.7 Hz AC; upgraded to 30-tonne axle load by 2003 allowing 8,600-tonne ore trains; LKAB subsidiary Malmtrafik (MTAB/MTAS) hauls iron ore from Kiruna, Malmberget and Svappavaara mines to ice-free Port of Narvik (LKAB ore port capacity 25 Mt/yr) and Port of Luleå; ~10-12 daily ore trains each way on Northern Circuit; first ore train Kiruna-Narvik 15 Nov 1902; full Narvik-Luleå electrification completed 1923 (then Europe's longest electric line); Ofotbanen is Norway's only rail link to Narvik - not connected to rest of national network; also carries CargoNet Arctic Rail Express containers + Vy passenger night train. WATCH (verified 05-Sep-2026): 60-page study prepared for the European Parliament Committee on Foreign Affairs (reported 04-Sep-2026 by tu.no, fremover.no, portseurope.com) recommends EU funding to fast-track upgrades of the Kiruna-Narvik rail-port-logistics corridor as a critical-minerals supply route and upgrading it to strategic status under the EU raw-materials framework; also calls for a permanent EU Arctic unit within the European Commission and closer EU cooperation with Norway, Iceland and Greenland (possible Canada/UK participation). European Commission/Parliament follow-up decision = next milestone. Primary document located 05-Sep-2026: European Parliament study "Focus on the High North: Upgrading the EU's Arctic policy and protecting the EU's interests in a rapidly evolving region" (EXAS_STU(2026)783620, requested by AFET committee, 60 pp, official PDF europarl.europa.eu) — explicitly recommends "stimulate the Kiruna-Narvik supply corridor: fund and fast-track integrated rail, port and multimodal logistics upgrades (EU Trans-European Transport Network co-funding, CRMA strategic project label) to link Kiruna mines to Narvik port for year-round ore export"; co-funding committed Q4 2026 timeline in study action table; also calls for permanent EU Arctic unit in Commission + closer EU cooperation with Norway/Iceland/Greenland. Commission/Parliament follow-up decision = next milestone.
eligibility: Freight infrastructure: operators require Norwegian/Swedish rail permits (LKAB Malmtrafik, Kaunis Iron, CargoNet, Vy); open-access regime under Bane NOR / Trafikverket
operator: LKAB Malmtrafik i Kiruna AB (MTAB) + Malmtrafikk AS (MTAS); infrastructure owners Bane NOR (Norway) and Trafikverket (Sweden)
status: Operational year-round (in service since 1902; 30t axle load since 2003)
sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ofoten_Line (43 km, Bane NOR ownership, Malmtrafik operations, 25 Mt/yr Narvik ore port); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LKAB_Malmtrafik (MTAB/MTAS structure, 15 kV electrification, 30t axle upgrade NOK 180M context); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Ore_Line (398 km Malmbanan, Trafikverket owner, 8,600t trains, 11-13 daily Northern Circuit); visitnarvik.com official destination page (10-12 daily ore trains, 68 wagons x 100t); nordnorge.com official Visit Northern Norway (first ore train 15 Nov 1902, most northerly standard-gauge point in Western Europe); museumnord.no (1923 electrification history, Porjus hydropower). program_name: Taksimo–Mirny transport corridor 'Vostochno-Sibirskaya khorda' (East Siberian Chord) — multimodal BAM↔NSR link, Irkutsk Oblast × Sakha (Yakutia)
city: Bodaybo, Irkutsk Oblast (mid-corridor hub; route Taksimo–Kropotkin–Bodaybo–Lensk–Mirny)
program_type: Interregional multimodal transport corridor program (road + rail + river)
key_benefits: Year-round road/rail connection from BAM station Taksimo (Buryatia) to Mirny (Sakha/Yakutia) via Kropotkin–Bodaybo–Lensk, replacing seasonal winter-road (zimnik) link via federal highway Vilyuy; scope: new highway Kropotkin–Lensk, capital repair Taksimo–Bodaybo–Kropotkin (Irkutsk Oblast) and Lensk–Mirny (Yakutia), modernization/expansion of Taksimo rail station on BAM; multimodal river–road–rail scheme effectively linking the Northern Sea Route with BAM; year-round access to East Siberia/Yakutia resource bases (gold, oil, gas, diamonds); joint working group for route selection, financing sources and environmental monitoring; Apr-2026: Yakutia PM K. Bychkov × RF Transport Deputy Minister I. Kostyuchenko (First International Transport & Logistics Forum, St. Petersburg) agreed to propose corridor 'Irkutsk–Taksimo–Kropotkin–Lensk–Mirny' for inclusion in the federal infrastructure modernization plan; Lensky bridge at Lensk/Yakutsk under construction in parallel (cable-stayed, first major crossing on permafrost; concession Group VIS x Sakha gov, natproj 'Infrastructure for Life', financing model approved by Putin; start Oct-2024): pier No.4 left bank fully concreted incl. pile cap Oct-2025 (Trutnev inspection 07-Oct-2025; payback 15-20 yrs via Severny zavoz flows); spring-2026 pile-cap concreting piers No.5-6 of 4.3 km left-bank approach (pier 5 = A360 'Lena' connection, 21 bored piles, 23 m; sakha.gov.ru); Jun-2026 central-pylon cofferdam No.9 (largest of 3) moved into channel after ice-out — 26/26 wall panels assembled, 97% guide pipes for 208 bored piles 1.5 m dia up to 40 m deep; 2026 plan per Mintrans Yakutia: 3 estakade piers + pile foundations on 13 right-bank piers, pontoon crossing, approach earthworks; federal dotations 41.6 bn RUB 2026-2028 (transport minister Sivtsev 27-Nov-2025); head of Sakha Nikolaev site check 23-24 Jul-2026 (RG); commissioning 2028; approach 5.5 km; regional accessibility 20.9%→83% projected; corridor investment volume not yet disclosed

program_name: Second Severomuysky Tunnel (SMT-2) — 15.3 km single-track BAM bore started 02-Sep-2026 by President Putin at VEF-2026; section capacity 16M→100M t/yr (BAM Eastern Polygon modernization Phase-3 key facility)
city: Severomuysk, Buryatia (eastern portal; North Muya Range / Novaya Chara valley section of BAM)
program_type: Federal railway capacity megaproject (BAM/Trans-Siberian Eastern Polygon modernization, third phase)
key_benefits: New 15.3 km single-track rail tunnel bored parallel to the 1975-2003 first Severomuysky Tunnel, eliminating the steep 64 km Severomuysky bypass (obkhod); raises throughput of the corridor section from 16 million to 100 million tonnes/yr and, with Trans-Sib, unlocks up to 270 Mt/yr eastern export capacity per project proponents. Investment 340.7 bn RUB excl. VAT, private-funded without budget money (initiative of Group Sibantstsit / УК VostokUgol; 2024 contract RZD x GK Bamtonnelstroy-Most per presidential instruction; Robbins TBMs). Trade-lane relevance: BAM is the southern feeder of the NSR — the ARC-RAIL-013 Taksimo-Mirny BAM↔NSR corridor's western anchor (Taksimo) sits on this section; expanded anthracite/coal + mineral export capacity underpins Asia-Pacific flows (Sibantstsit/VostokUgol premium coal) and BAM-routed cargo incl. Elga coal field. NAME-DISAMBIG: Second Severomuysky Tunnel != first Severomuysky Tunnel (operational since 2003) != Severomuysky bypass road/rail obkhod; distinct project from ARC-RAIL-013 Taksimo-Mirny corridor (intersects at Taksimo node) and from Lensky bridge (ARC-RAIL-013 update, Lena crossing near Yakutsk).
eligibility: n/a — RZD/private-investor megaproject; tunneling, TBMs and civil-works supply chain
operator: RZD (infrastructure owner) + OOO 'Severomuysky Tunnel-2' (Group Sibantstsit / УК VostokUgol) investor-operator company; GK Bamtonnelstroy-Most construction contract (2024); The Robbins Company TBM supply
